newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: ICE HOCKEY-CZECHS NAME CO-COACHES FOR WORLD TOURNEY.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CZECHS NAME CO-COACHES FOR WORLD TOURNEY.

text.p: World champions the Czech Republic on Wednesday named Slavomir Lener and Ivan Hlinka as co-coaches of the national team for the world championship starting next month in Helsinki.
An official from the Czech Ice Hockey Federation said Sparta Prague coach Lener, and Litvinov's Hlinka would jointly lead the team, replacing Ludek Bukac who resigned last week.
Bukac, who replaced Hlinka as national team coach in 1994, said last Friday that he was quitting following a widening rift between himself and several key players.

Since becoming coach in 1994 Bukac has driven out many top players, but he managed to guide the Czechs last year to their first world championship since the former Czechoslovakia won the last of six titles in 1985.
In recent weeks he has come under intense criticism from the media after public disputes with NHL leading goalscorer Jaromir Jagr and top Czech club goaltender Roman Cechmanek.

Hlinka returns to the helm of the national team after leading the last Czechoslovak national team before the split of the country in 1993 and a disappointing stint as coach of the first Czech-only Olympic team in Norway in 1994.
Hlinka played in several Czechoslovak world championship and Olympic teams in the 1970s.
His Litvinov club have fallen to ninth in the first division standings after a second place finish in 1996.
Sparta, the strongest Prague-based club team, have struggled lately but are still second in the first division.
Since winning the world championship in Vienna, the Czech national team have won only three of 18 games, including an embarrassing 7-1 defeat to Germany in a Canadian international tournament.
